title: 2026 WNBA Finals: Game 6 location up in the air for Dream vs. Valkyries - CBS Sports
description: The Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to play at State Farm Arena on Thursday night, which leaves the Dream scrambling
body:
The Atlanta Hawks are scheduled to play at State Farm Arena on Thursday night, which leaves the Dream scrambling for an alternative
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Valkyries held off the Atlanta Dream's comeback attempt on Saturday to secure a 67-62 win in Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals. The result evened the series at 2-2 and ensured that the series will return to Atlanta for Game 6 -- though where, specifically, remains to be seen. The location for Game 6 on Thursday is still officially listed as "TBD" on the schedule due to a conflict with State Farm Arena. The Atlanta Hawks, State Farm Arena's primary tenant, are scheduled to host the Cleveland Cavaliers that night. Tip-off for the Hawks game is set for 7 p.m. ET, while tip-off for Game 6 is set for 8 p.m. ET. Obviously, State Farm Arena cannot host two games at the same time, which means one or both of the games will have to be adjusted. The WNBA did not have an update to share when reached for comment by CBS Sports. "We are waiting to hear from the league if any changes can be made to allow us to play in State Farm Arena. If not, the game will be played in Gateway Center Arena," a Dream spokesperson told ESPN. 
Gateway Center Arena in College Park, the Dream's primary home, is the league's smallest venue, with a capacity of just 3,500. That is not an ideal setting for a Finals game -- or any playoff game -- and the Dream have played all five of their postseason contests at State Farm Arena. That included Games 3 and 4 of the Finals, which had to be moved due to other conflicts. Game 3 was moved from Oct. 22 to Oct. 21 to avoid a Sombr concert, while Game 4 was moved up to 1 p.m. ET to accommodate the Hawks' home opener against the Houston Rockets on Saturday; the NBA game was shifted back to 8:30 p.m. ET. There is less flexibility for both parties moving forward, however, so it's still unclear what will happen with Game 6. Here's a closer look at the options:Move Game 6 to Wednesday: This is not possible because the Hawks are also at home that night against the Miami Heat.Move the Hawks-Cavaliers game to Friday: The Hawks also play on Wednesday, but are off on Friday before playing again on Saturday. The Cavaliers, the Hawks' opponent on Thursday, are also off Friday before playing again on Saturday. State Farm Arena has an open date for Friday, but Friday nights are supposed to be NBA Cup exclusive games. Move the Hawks-Cavaliers game to Cleveland: Could the NBA, the Hawks and the Cavaliers agree to reverse Thursday's fixture and play it in Cleveland? The idea has been considered, per ESPN, but, like moving the Hawks-Cavaliers game to Friday, would create major logistical issues that multiple franchises, the NBA and broadcast partners would have to sign off on. Play a doubleheader: The Dream and Hawks played a doubleheader at State Farm on Saturday. Could they do it again on Thursday? Again, the Hawks play on Wednesday, so they could not turn around and play on Thursday afternoon. Thus, any doubleheader would require Game 6 to be played in the afternoon, and the WNBA is reportedly not fond of having a weekday matinee Finals game. Play Game 6 at Gateway Center: This is the easiest solution. It would not be ideal to host Game 6 of the Finals at a 3,500-seat venue, but Gateway Center is the Dream's primary home and there would be no logistical challenges. Play Game 6 at another arena in Atlanta: The Dream could try to move Game 6 to another venue in Atlanta. But where? Gas South Arena holds 13,000, but has a concert scheduled for Thursday. McCamish Pavilion on Georgia Tech's campus -- where the Dream played for two seasons from 2017-18 -- holds 8,600 and has an open date on Thursday. The Georgia State Convocation Center holds 7,500 and appears to have an open date on Thursday as well. Those would be the two best options if the WNBA and the Dream want a bigger crowd, but the Dream haven't played at either venue this season. Would they want to play the biggest game of their season at an unfamiliar venue? Make a major adjustment to the Finals schedule: A radical option would be to shift Game 6 to Friday, which is an open date on the State Farm calendar, and then move Game 7, if necessary, to Tuesday, Nov. 3 at Chase Center in San Francisco. This would potentially mean three days off between both Games 5 and 6 and Games 6 and 7, however. The WNBA would reportedly support this proposal, but it would require sign-off from both teams as well as other partners, and the Valkyries have raised concerns. After Game 4, Angel Reese made it clear that she hopes the WNBA can find a way to get Game 6 at State Farm Arena. Here's her exchange with a reporter during the postgame press conference:
Question: It took quite a bit to get these Games 3 and 4 moved here, and now that you know you will need a Game 6, what's your hope or expectation of what that would look like coming back to Atlanta?Reese: Just them showing up again. The fan support here has been amazing. We appreciate the love and support and everybody coming out. And being able to force a Game 6 at least. Being able to come here and play in front of the home crowd again would be amazing.Question: Here or Gateway?Reese: HereEarlier this month, the Dream announced a multi-year deal to play all home games at State Farm Arena, starting with the 2027 season, thereby avoiding any such conflicts in the future. Unfortunately for them, that doesn't solve the Game 6 dilemma.

Hardy hasn't played in 2026 while recovering gunshot wound he suffered in the offseason
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:18 pm ET

            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Eli Drinkwitz gave Missouri fans some great news on Sunday evening. Star running back Ahmad Hardy will return to practice this week after recovering from a gunshot wound he suffered in the offseason, the school announced Sunday.Back in May, Hardy was shot in the upper leg while attending a concert in Mississippi. He was taken to the hospital for emergency surgery, and he hasn't seen the field at all this season due to his recovery.Earlier this season, Drinkwitz was asked about Hardy's progress, and he promised that he would announced when the star running back returned to practice."I really don't want to have to answer that question every week, and I will tell y'all when there is an update," Drinkwitz said. "... There's no update. He hasn't began a two-week ramp-up period. If he practices, I promise I'll tweet it out. I won't even give it to Pete. We'll just do it ourselves."
Drinkwitz made good on his promise Sunday, although Hardy's status for Saturday's game against Arkansas is still unknown.
Hardy was arguably the best running back in the country last season as he led all Power Four player with 1,649 rushing yards and 16 rushing touchdowns.With Hardy out due to his rehab, Jamal Roberts has filled in nicely for the Tigers. Roberts ranks seventh in the country with 867 rushing yards, and his eight rushing touchdowns are tied for 18th. If Missouri can get Hardy back to anything resembling the player he was last season, it will have the best running back tandem in the nation.
The Tigers may be able to let Hardy ramp up this week, but they have to be eyeing a return for a November home stretch that includes Texas, Georgia, Kentucky and Oklahoma. Missouri's offense will need as much help as it can get against those defenses.

        With one week left until the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, no team is safe from the chaos. That is reflected in the spreads for some of Week 9's biggest matchups.One of the bigger spreads in top-25 matchups is Georgia going to Atlanta as a two-score favorite against Florida. The Bulldogs entered their open date on a low note with a devastating loss to Auburn, but the Gators were riding high on the heels of a top-10 win over Texas in Austin.With Julian Sayin sidlined by an injury, Ohio State goes into Los Angeles to take on a mentally wounded USC team, which just fell to unranked Wisconsin. In spite of their big question at quarterback, the Buckeyes opened as favorites against the Trojans.There are just three unbeaten teams remaining in college football -- Miami, Utah and UCLA. The Hurricanes and Bruins are massive favorites in Week 9, but the Utes face a tricky road trip to Cincinnati.
Let's take a look at the schedule and early lines.Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.The big gamesFlorida vs. Georgia (-10.5): This is technically a neutral-site game, although the crowd at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta will probably lean red-and-black. Both teams are coming off an open date, but the way each entered the off week couldn't be more different. Florida went into Austin with its backup quarterback and rallied for a comeback win over No. 7 Texas. Georgia suffered a stunning upset at the hands of rival Auburn, knocking the Bulldogs from their spot atop atop the rankings. Despite that, the oddsmakers see the Dawgs as an obvious favorite.Ohio State (-7) at USC: It doesn't necessarily reflect well upon Lincoln Riley that Ohio State is a touchdown favorite in Los Angeles despite starting a backup quarterback. It's not hard to see why this line is what it is after watching the Trojans struggle to move the ball against Wisconsin in a 24-7 loss to the Badgers on Saturday night. Star quarterback Jayden Maiava looked pedestrian, and while the USC defense played well enough to win, Wisconsin doesn't have anyone remotely like Heisman Trophy favorite Jeremiah Smith on their roster.Arizona at Texas Tech (-4.5): The Wildcats have very quietly rolled to a 6-1 start, and their lone loss was an 11-point defeat in Provo. Now, they will faced a frustrated Texas Tech team in Lubbock. The Red Raiders got beaten rather convincingly by Cincinnati, 37-24, in Week 8. Will Hammond continues to struggle at quarterback. Super booster Cody Campbell is tweeting about it being an inxecusable loss. If Texas Tech can't regroup and pull itself together, Arizona is more than capable of handing the Red Raiders their second straight loss. The winner's Big 12 and College Football Playoff chances will get a nice boost.
Wisconsin at Iowa (-3.5): After losing the battle for the Floyd of Rosedale -- a 98-pound bronze pig -- Iowa will get an immediate shot at redemption this week. The Hawkeyes and Badgers will play for the Heartland Trophy, a 72-pound brass bull. Which trophy is more prestigious? Your answer depends on your preference between pork and beef. While Iowa just suffered a heartbreaking last-minute loss to Minnesota, Wisconsin is riding high after picking up a top-25 win over USC, and the Badgers are 3-1 in Big Ten play.Minnesota at Indiana (-20.5): Despite Minnesota's win over Iowa and Indiana's struggles against Michigan, the oddsmakers don't have much faith in the Golden Gophers. To be fair, Minnesota hasn't given anyone much reason to trust it this fall with a 25-point loss to Mississippi State and a 28-point loss to Purdue on its resume. Still, the Hoosiers haven't made life easy on themselves lately. They needed overtime to beat a Michigan team that was starting freshman Tommy Carr at quarterback, and Josh Hoover threw for just 81 yards.Utah (-6.5) at Cincinnati: One week after handing Texas Tech its first loss of the season, Cincinnati has the chance to take down another unbeaten Big 12 opponent. The Bearcats rode their running game and an opportunistic defense to a win in Nippert Stadium on Saturday, but can they do that twice in a row? The Utes are coming off a hard-fought top-25 win over Houston late Saturday night, and it makes you wonder whether they could be the next team victimized the dreaded road trip immediately following an emotional win. Vegas certainly doesn't think Utah will roll into Cincinnati and run away with this game.

body:
The 2026-27 college football coaching carousel is in full swing, and these teams will have to pony up to pay off their former coaches
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Baylor became the third Power Four program to fire its head coach on Sunday when it dismissed Dave Aranda after seven seasons. Baylor joined North Carolina State and Maryland as the coaching carousel finally got spinning in late October. With each firing comes a high financial cost to move on from the coach. What is each school paying to fire its coach, and where could it go next? CBS Sports breaks it down below.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    BaylorFired coach: Dave Aranda (40-40 in 7 seasons)Cost: Reportedly $12 millionBaylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday following disappointing losses to TCU and Kansas. Aranda had seemingly cooled his seat with a 4-1 start, but those losses ultimately doomed him. As a private school, Baylor does not release coaching contracts the way public schools must. The buyout figure was believed to be approximately $12 million last season, while Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger reported that same figure for this year's cost. Candidates to replace Aranda include Boise State's Spencer Danielson and UTSA's Jeff Traylor. Check out the full list of Baylor coaching options here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    MarylandFired coach: Mike Locksley (39-54 in 8 seasons)
Cost: $9.75 million Maryland kicked off the coaching carousel when it fired Mike Locksley on Wednesday. The school owes Locksley around $9.75 million with no offsets if he takes another job. Half of that $9.75 million is due to Locksley within sixty days. He had been under contract through 2028 but was let go after a 2-5 start to the season, which included losses to Rutgers, Virginia Tech and UCLA. Candidates to replace Locksley include Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, New Mexico's Jason Eck and Memphis' Charles Huff. Full candidates list here. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    North Carolina StateFired coach: Dave Doeren (98-73 in 14 seasons)Cost: $10.3 million NC State opted for a rare Saturday afternoon firing when it dumped Dave Doeren after 14 seasons. There had been rumblings before the season that this could be Doeren's last in Raleigh, but that was centered around a possible retirement and not a firing. Instead, NC State will pay approximately $10.3 million to buy out the remainder of a contract set to run through 2029. NC State owes Doeren a little more than $600,000 within the next 30 days, and can then pay the remainder in monthly installments. The 54-year-old Doeren does have a clause in his contract requiring him to make reasonable efforts to find another job, which could offset the buyout NC State owes. 
The early candidate to watch to replace Doeren is former NC State quarterback great Philip Rivers. More on Rivers and NC State here.

Be careful touting signature wins too early during college football season.Paper champions loading up on early victories can easily be extinguished by midseason when inflated schedules come to a grinding halt during conference play. We've seen it happen across the SEC, Big Ten and now Big 12, following the league's wildest weekend yet.There's the flip side too -- teams can get hot and find their footing after the opening month, strengthening an opponent's resume thanks to a prior result.The current AP Top 25 rankings give us a snapshot of which wins have aged well and which are depreciating assets ahead of the first College Football Playoff poll on Nov. 3. Beating a top-10 team in September that later disappears from the rankings doesn't preserve a ranked victory on that résumé. With the postseason picture taking shape, it's time to revisit some of the memorable results from earlier this fall. 
These are the squads who banked something meaningful and those in search of more approaching the final month of the campaign.Wins that aged wellNo. 12 Alabama 45, Kentucky 17When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Kentucky's current ranking: No. 9The Crimson Tide handled the SEC's current leader its only loss this season by four touchdowns and did so despite multiple first-half turnovers and a halftime deficit. Alabama outscored Kentucky 32-0 in the second half, and guess what? The Wildcats haven't lost since. That's one of the most insane rebounds in SEC history for a first-year coaching staff. The victory was Alabama's ninth straight over Kentucky and marks the Crimson Tide's lone win over a team currently ranked in the top 25.No. 4 Texas 24, No. 1 Ohio State 23When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Ohio State's current ranking: No. 2If Texas finds itself in the middle of the SEC's nine-win pack a few weeks from now, the Longhorns will have something others do not -- one of the best nonconference victories of the season. Everyone knew that the 20-point comeback win over Ohio State would carry significant weight, and the Buckeyes are one of only two unbeaten teams in Big Ten play.
The Buckeyes' season could torpedo from here without Julian Sayin given what's left on the schedule, but that's not the expectation. Ohio State is confident in its quarterback room behind Sayin and has a Heisman candidate who can bail this offense out of difficult spots when the ball's thrown in his direction.No. 13 Texas Tech 28, No. 22 Houston 26When: Sept. 18 (Week 3)Houston's current ranking: No. 18Cougars coach Willie Fritz put it succinctly after his team's narrow loss in Lubbock in mid-September, where a failed two-point conversion in the final moments proved the difference. "There's no moral victories," Fritz said after losing to Texas Tech last month. "We came here to win. And we didn't win."
Houston's 4-1 since that setback after its four-game winning streak was snapped Saturday night at Utah. This remains Texas Tech's only ranked win, with another opportunity coming in Week 9 against Arizona.No. 5 Miami 33, Wake Forest 20When: Sept. 19 (Week 3)Wake Forest's current ranking: No. 14The Demon Deacons are arguably the ACC's second-best team on the heels of four consecutive wins entering next weekend's home game against Virginia. Their only loss in league play is to the Hurricanes, and they've outscored their last three opponents, 132-24, in the ACC. Jake Dickert is getting the most out of UNC transfer quarterback Gio Lopez (17 touchdowns, one interception) and Wake Forest controls its own destiny in the race for a spot in the ACC Championship Game.Miami's Darian Mensah completed an ACC-record 24 straight passes in this victory as the Hurricanes jumped out to a 31-7 lead midway through the third quarter behind his brilliance and early success with Malachi Toney. Miami dominated this road matchup for three quarters, but the final score doesn't reflect how one-sided it really was.
No. 4 Notre Dame 41, Wisconsin 13When: Sept. 6 (Week 1)Wisconsin's current ranking: No. 25No one knew if the Badgers would recover after flatlining at Lambeau Field against the Fighting Irish during Labor Day weekend, but Wisconsin did show some unexpected fight in that one for 2.5 quarters to open a pivotal campaign for Luke Fickell. Wisconsin's only loss since was last week's 17-7 setback at UCLA, as Saturday night's win over 16th-ranked USC pushed the Badgers to 5-2 overall.No. 12 Kentucky 35, No. 18 LSU 34When: Oct. 10 (Week 6)LSU's current ranking: No. 15The second of consecutive overtime wins for Will Stein and the Wildcats this season, Kenny Minchey called his own number on the game-winning quarterback draw, sending Kroger Field into a frenzy. LSU is unbeaten since, with consecutive blowout wins against SEC opponents, to pull back inside the top-15. These are two of four SEC playoff picks in our latest bowl projections, and there's a chance each finishes with 10 wins. Who would've predicted that for the boys in blue three months ago?No. 15 BYU 28, Arizona 17When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Arizona's current ranking: No. 20In the Big 12 opener for both teams, the Cougars erased a 17-14 halftime deficit, scoring a pair of touchdowns after intermission to prevail as the only defense to quiet the Wildcats up to this point. Arizona improved to 6-1 overall after Saturday's victory over Iowa State and is now ranked. Quarterback Noah Fifita has given opposing defenses problems the last four seasons and gets a chance to cause chaos with upcoming contests against Texas Tech and Utah down the stretch. BYU would love for Arizona to play spoiler and make its road to the playoff that much clearer.
Wins that aged poorlyKentucky 31, No. 9 Texas A&M 21When: Sept. 19 (Week 3)Texas A&M's current ranking: NRDozens of Kentucky fans were in my mentions this week asking why the Wildcats weren't included in our group of five teams with at least two ranked wins this season. That's because their team's demolition of the Aggies at Kyle Field was the beginning of the end for Texas A&M's place in the top 25. The Aggies, now 4-4 overall,  were our most overrated team in the preseason top-10 and proved that quickly this fall after replacing several starters in the trenches and having no answer for the loss of KC Concepcion at wideout. Kentucky simply exposed glaring issues before anyone else could.No. 7 Alabama 56, No. 16 Mississippi State 23When: Oct. 3 (Week 5)Mississippi State's current ranking: NRHanding Kamario Taylor and the Bulldogs their first loss of the season was a memorable road beatdown in Starkville, but Mississippi State hasn't won a game since and has tumbled outside of the national rankings. The Bulldogs were shut out by LSU, struggled at home in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma and now travel to Texas on Halloween. Keelon Russell's four total touchdowns in this game pushed him toward the front of the Heisman race before those hopes evaporated after losses to Georgia and Tennessee.Michigan 17, No. 11 Oklahoma 10When: Sept. 12 (Week 2)Oklahoma's current ranking: NRSo much for the Wolverines using their promising start under Kyle Whittingham. They've moved on from Bryce Underwood as their starting quarterback. Then, Tommy Carr's first career start resulted in a six-point dud during Saturday's overtime loss to Indiana. Michigan's defense remains this team's calling card, but the Wolverines are not scoring enough points to keep pace in the Big Ten or CFP races.
No. 9 Ole Miss 41, No. 24 Louisville 38When: Sept. 6 (Week 1)Louisville's current ranking: NRLouisville was believed to be a title contender this season in the ACC considering Jeff Brohm had registered 29 total wins his first three years with the Cardinals, but a 4-3 start has left much to be desired in the middle of the conference. Consecutive losses to Wake Forest and NC State eliminated Louisville from legitimate league title hopes and exposed the real issue for this team - they can't stop anyone. Ranked in the lower third of the ACC in total, scoring and pass defense, the Cardinals can blame themselves for this rapid deterioration. Heading into Week 8, the only countable ranked wins for Ole Miss were LSU and Missouri.Northwestern 34, Penn State 13When: Oct. 2 (Week 5)Penn State's current ranking: NRDon't tell any Northwestern folks this win lacked significance. At the time, the first game at the new $875 million Ryan Field was a memorable one after the Wildcats galloped their way to 413 yards rushing, but the Nittany Lions have completely flatlined since. Winless in the Big Ten after four games, this was Matt Campbell's second crack at a conference opponent after losing at home to Wisconsin the previous week. Northwestern's now ranked and 6-1 overall after Saturday's win over Rutgers, but the next three games will ultimately determine this team's value against Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State.Colorado 14, Georgia Tech 13When: Sept. 3 (Week 1)Georgia Tech's current ranking: NRDoes anyone still remember this one? Both of these teams stink and will need strong second halves of the campaign just to get bowl-eligible. Deion Sanders and the Buffaloes have lost five straight following Saturday night's 57-24 beatdown from Oklahoma State, while the Yellow Jackets are 1-5 this season against Power Four competition, the lone victory coming against Duke on Oct. 10.
Virginia 34, NC State 8When: Aug. 29 (Week 0)NC State's current ranking: NRAn opening-weekend game many thought would determine part of the top-end ACC standings turned out to be pretty much meaningless. Virginia lost at home to Duke on Friday night, falling to 4-4 on the year, hours before NC State's loss at Stanford marked the end of Dave Doeren's tenure as leader of the program. The second Power Four vacancy this cycle, the Wolfpack will have a search for the first time in 14 years after moving on from the ACC's second longest-tenured coach.

title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey exits with injury vs. Falcons, is questionable to return - CBS Sports
description: The Niners can breathe a sigh of relief with CMC back on the field
body:
The Niners can breathe a sigh of relief with CMC back on the field
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026

    3:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has returned to the game against the Atlanta Falcons after going to the locker room with a thigh injury. He was initially listed as questionable, but he was able to come back on the first drive of the third quarter.McCaffrey seemed to aggravate his leg during the first quarter, but he went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter before leaving for the locker room. Before going down with the injury, CMC had four carries for 29 yards and one touchdown in the first half. He added a carry for a loss of two yards in the first attempt back from the locker room. He also has three receptions for 45 yards in the air. So far this season, he has 77 carries for 350 yards and seven touchdowns on the ground, along with 28 receptions for 190 yards in the air through six games. 
McCaffrey is a dual-threat running back in quarterback Brock Purdy's offense and a reliable pass catcher. However, the 30-year-old has a history of injuries. The former Comeback Player of the Year had a PCL sprain, which sidelined him for five games in 2024; a pedal Achilles sprain that sidelined him for eight games the same year; a left calf strain that caused him to miss one game in 2023; and a pedal ankle sprain and thigh hamstring strain each sidelined him for five games in 2021.
The 49ers offense is already without wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Demarcus Robinson (IR), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR) and Ricky Pearsall (IR). McCaffrey is a crucial part of this 49ers offense and having him back on the field is great news for the Niners and their fans. The running back room also includes rookie Kaelon Black and second-year RB Jordan James. Black currently leads the team in carries (11) and rushing yards (60) against Atlanta. McCaffrey leads the team in carries and rushing yards this season, with Black behind him and their QB third on the list.With the exception of 2024, when he was limited to four games due to injury, McCaffrey has led the team in rushing yards, including two 1,000-plus yard seasons. 
In his 10-year career, he has 1,735 rushes for 7,939 yards and 69 rushing touchdowns. McCaffrey was drafted in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft, when the Carolina Panthers took him at No. 8 overall. He remained in the Queen City until 2022, when he joined the 49ers. The Niners are currently down 19-14 against the Falcons as San Fran looks to stay undefeated. CBS Sports will continue to update this article as more information becomes available.

title: With a historically low number of undefeated teams left, 2026 is poised for a frenzied finish - CBS Sports
description: Undefeated teams are dropping like flies every week in a 2026 season teeming with upsets
body:
Undefeated teams are dropping like flies every week in a 2026 season teeming with upsets
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:31 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Halloween is still six days away, and undefeated teams are dropping like flies in college football. With No. 2 BYU's loss to UCF and No. 8 Texas Tech's loss to Cincinnati, just three unbeatens remain in FBS, a historic low.The last time major college football had only three undefeated teams through Oct. 24 was in 1977. I'd let you guess which teams those were, but we might be here all week, and I have another full slate of action to cover on Saturday.Through Oct. 24, 1977, Texas was sitting at 6-0, and its unblemished brethren were Colgate (7-0) and Louisiana Tech (4-0-2). So, yes, it's extremely rare to have this much carnage at this point in the season.The only three teams with a zero in the loss column are Miami, Utah and UCLA. The Hurricanes are a serious candidate to run the table -- at least in the regular season, but the other two are much more vulnerable.
After notching a top-25 win over Houston late Saturday night, Utah must travel to Cincinnati, which just handed Texas Tech its first loss of the season. After that, it's Holy War time as BYU visits Salt Lake City.The Bruins are playing with a backup quarterback for the rest of the season, and they still have to visit Minnesota and Michigan before hosting USC. It's a manageable path for UCLA, but the loss of Nico Iamaleava reduces the team's margin for error on a weekly basis.If you think all three of those remaining unbeatens will get through the rest of the season unscathed, you haven't been watching much college football in 2026. In fact, there's a chance we don't have any undefeated teams if Miami loses to Notre Dame on Nov. 7.
All this parity is setting up for a wild November filled with neck-and-neck conference races and maddening College Football Playoff debates. I can't wait.Perplexing playoff pictureWe've already seen 2007-level insanity, and there's still one week of games left before the first College Football Playoff rankings are unveiled on Tuesday, Nov. 3.The race for the playoffs is officially wide open because as small as the number of undefeated teams is, the list of one-loss teams is shrinking rapidly too. There are only 16 teams with one or fewer losses on their resumes, and just 12 of those reside in a Power Four conference.
As a result, the list of teams with hope of reaching the College Football Playoff is lengthy. According to ESPN FPI, there are 19 teams with at least a 20 percent chance (or 1-in-5 shot) of getting into the playoff field. And that doesn't even include one-loss teams like Arizona or SMU.It should also be noted that two of the teams with a better-than-50-percent chance, Texas and Alabama, already have two losses. Will both of those teams run the table? Given what we've seen to this point, that seems unlikely.What about two-loss teams with big-game opportunities coming up? USC plays a shorthanded Ohio State team in Los Angeles this weekend, and the path really widens for the winner of Iowa vs. Wisconsin on Saturday.
The evolution of NIL and the transfer portal has created a new era of parity in college football, and that's great news for fans, but it will create some tough decisions for the playoff selection committee.I don't envy anyone on that committee because someone with a legitimate case to reach the playoff will get left out. There are too many participants and too few seats in this game of musical chairs.Conference title game chaosWith the CFP set to expand to 24 teams next year, this will likely be our final season with conference championship games, at least among the Power Four leagues.
If they're going extinct, they may as well go out with a bang, and these conference championship races are shaping up for exactly that. Just look around the country at some of these conference standings.In the SEC, first-place Kentucky is rolling toward a matchup against Georgia. The Wildcats have never appeared in an SEC title game before, but it would be better late than never if they can sneak in a trip to Atlanta under the wire.What about the Big Ten? A rematch between Ohio State and Indiana is far from a lock at this point. Neither team has looked invulnerable, and each has its own unique quarterback issue. There's also the matter of UCLA -- a team that went 3-9 last year -- sitting in first place at 5-0 in conference play, and the Bruins may not play another ranked team.
Now let's check in on the Big 12, where your guess about what will happen week to week is as good as mine. Utah is the clear front-runner, at least for now, but the Utes still have to play Cincinnati, BYU and Arizona. Behind Utah, there are four teams with one conference loss just waiting for the Utes to slip up.We can all admit that Miami is running away with the ACC, although the Hurricanes haven't won the conference title game since coming over from the Big East. The race for second place in the ACC is what's really fascinating. Wake Forest and SMU each have one loss, but Virginia Tech and Louisville are on their heels at 3-2. It helps that the Cardinals already have a head-to-head win over the Mustangs.I hope everyone is up to date on conference tiebreakers because they will almost certainly come into play once we make it through Thanksgiving weekend. We still have five weeks of these teams eating one another alive, and it will be a joy to watch.

        Just when the Texas offense got back on track against Ole Miss, it lost one of its best players. Left tackle Trevor Goosby has suffered a season-ending knee injury, multiple outlets report.Goosby went down during the first quarter of the Longhorns' 34-27 win over the Rebels on Saturday night, and he was carted off the field. After undergoing evaluation in the locker room, Goosby returned to the sideline on crutches.The loss of Goosby is a massive one for the Horns, a team that has struggled to find consistency on offense. A fourth-year tackle, Goosby is considered one of the top offensive linemen in the country, and he projects as a first-round NFL Draft pick.Not only does Goosby bring experience to the offensive line with 22 starts over the last three seasons, but he has the talent and accolades to go along with it. Goosby earned All-SEC honors in 2025, and he was a preseason first-team All-American at CBS Sports.
In the immediate aftermath of the Ole Miss game, Sarkisian couldn't provide updates on Goosby or star wide receiver Cam Coleman, both of whom suffered what appeared to be significant injuries."Well, I think, I don't have all the particulars on Cam (Coleman) and Trevor (Goosby)," Sarkisian said. "Obviously, neither of them look very good."Andre Cojoe replaced Goosby at left tackle, and he did an admirable job in relief as Ole Miss sacked Arch Manning just twice. Although Cojoe hasn't played as many games as Goosby, he is a senior who has been in the program since he signed with the Longhorns in 2023.
Cojoe missed the entire 2025 season due to injury, but he has appeared in all seven games this season and 11 total games throughout his career, albeit in a limited capacity.Texas has allowed 2.71 sacks per game, which is tied for 117th nationally, and it's hard to see that improving with Goosby on the shelf.The Longhorns must now prepare to be without their best offensive lineman and have zero margin for error in the College Football Playoff race. That test begins this weekend as Texas hosts Mississippi State on Saturday night.

title: Nikola Jokić calls out booing Nuggets fans: 'Not welcome anymore' - CBS Sports
description: Denver's home fans shared their displeasure as the Nuggets fell behind by more than 20 points to the Pelicans
body:
Denver's home fans shared their displeasure as the Nuggets fell behind by more than 20 points to the Pelicans
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        An NBA season hasn't truly begun until the Denver Nuggets have played with their food for three-and-a-half quarters, fallen behind by double digits, and then furiously rallied back for a comeback against an inferior opponent. It is among the most common game-style archetypes in the NBA, a quirk of Denver's that has lasted more or less Nikola Jokić's entire career. You'd think by now that the fans in Denver would understand that after watching it for more than a decade.Alas, Nuggets fans shared quite a bit of displeasure with the team when they fell behind by more than 20 in the first half against the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday. They rained boos down on their team, which was already winless after a tough loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder in the opener in which they were held to their fewest points in a regular-season game (84) since January 2024.Thereafter, the Nuggets did what they've so often done during the Jokić era. The Pelicans led by as many as 23, and were even up 16 with 7:24 remaining, but the Nuggets stormed back. They managed to force overtime by holding the Pelicans without a field goal attempt in the last 80 seconds of the game, and once they got to the extra period, they didn't look back in outscoring New Orleans 15-9 to seal the 141-135 victory. The same fans who booed in the first half serenaded rookie Trevon Brazile with MVP chants in overtime.Yet Jokić, Denver's actual three-time MVP, couldn't quite get over the wishy-washy behavior of his home fans. 
"We got booed at our first home game, and I think those fans who booed us, they don't need to come anymore," Jokić said. "If you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we've come back from much worse situations. So if they ask me, they are not welcome anymore."
Booing is a part of the game, and frankly, the Nuggets are coming off a stretch in which they've certainly made fans antsy enough to do so. Denver lost its first-round playoff series last spring despite facing a Timberwolves team riddled with injuries. The Nuggets then signed and traded breakout forward Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers in what was largely a financial decision. There was fear coming into the season that Denver's championship window around Jokić had truly closed, and a first-half beatdown at the hands of the lowly Pelicans seemingly confirmed that. Fans had more to boo than usual in Denver.Jokić did what he so often does and won anyway. As long as he's on the team, Denver will usually have a chance to do so. But fans might want to be cautious about invoking Jokić's ire this season. After all, he can become an unrestricted free agent next offseason. And while he's made it clear on several occasions that he intends to re-sign, his word isn't binding. 
The last thing Denver fans want is to boo Jokić out the door, so they might want to give the greatest player in franchise history a bit more benefit of the doubt than they did on Saturday.

title: Cam Skattebo redemption game: Giants' RB bounces back with 124-yard performance after benching - CBS Sports
description: Fresh out of the dog house, the second-year back erupted for 124 yards and set up Devin Singletary's overtime tou
body:
Fresh out of the dog house, the second-year back erupted for 124 yards and set up Devin Singletary's overtime touchdown to revive New York's run game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The much-maligned New York Giants running back room showed up in a big way during their Week 7, 27-21 overtime victory over the Houston Texans. Just one week after Cam Skattebo recorded zero carries in a one-score loss to the New Orleans Saints, he returned to the lineup and rushed for a career-high 124 yards and one touchdown on 17 carries.ESPN reported before the game that Skattebo was expected to take over the Giants' backfield after he was seemingly benched in Week 6 following a costly fumble in overtime of the Giants' Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders. Skattebo said he was "taught a lesson," and when overtime came this week, he was the hero instead of the disappointment. In the extra period, the second-year back broke loose for a 42-yard gain, which set up a Devin Singletary 30-yard game-winning touchdown. This made the Giants the only team in the past 35 years to register 30-plus yard runs on consecutive plays in overtime, per CBS Sports Research. The Giants had zero 30-yard rushes on their first 461 offensive plays this season. Sunday marked the first game since 1950 where the Giants saw four different players score rushing touchdowns, as Skattebo, Singletary, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Jameis Winston all found the end zone. 
The Giants really needed this performance. From John Harbaugh, to Skattebo, to the running back room at large. One week after New York's running backs combined for just 34 rushing yards, they hit 180 yards this week. The running back group was a major talking point after Najee Harris was booted from the team after being critical of Harbaugh's rotation. 
"It's hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays," Harris said, via The Trentonian. "The first couple runs will be like, 'OK, how are they playing it?' And then the next ones will be, 'OK, this is how you attack it.' But if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do. That's why I'm saying, 'I don't know.' I've never been through none of this before."Harbaugh told reporters he understood why Harris was frustrated, but maintained that playing time had to be earned. So did Harris' roster spot, apparently.  "I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities, and you're sure to get more opportunities. You know? Do something."
Skattebo said this past Friday that Harris' release proved "nobody's safe," including himself. While he established himself as a fan favorite during his rookie season, becoming one of just five players to rack up 400 rushing yards and 200 receiving yards through the first eight games of the season, he failed to rush for more than 60 yards in each of his past five games with zero touchdowns. With a new regime, Skattebo had to prove himself once again."I think when we go on the field, and we perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here," Skattebo said. "And if I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here."  It's safe to say Skattebo earned some points with Harbaugh and the staff on Sunday. The Texans entered Week 7 with the No. 3 rush defense in the NFL, allowing just 83 rushing yards per game. However, Skattebo out-physicaled DeMeco Ryans' unit in their own building this week. 
Week 7 could serve as a turning point for the 4-2-1 Giants. Not only did the rushing attack finally show up, but this was also the first start for new quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards while New York racked up 420 yards of total offense compared to the Texans' 237 total yards. The Giants are now the new favorites to win the wonky NFC East over at DraftKings Sportsbook (+110). The Giants will enjoy their bye week before traveling to Philadelphia to take on the rival Eagles on Nov. 8.

title: John Harbaugh's Giants improve to 4-2-1 as J.J. McCarthy, Cam Skattebo star in OT - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy impressed in his first start for New York, and Skattebo responded emphatically to his Week 6 benching
body:
McCarthy impressed in his first start for New York, and Skattebo responded emphatically to his Week 6 benching
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When J.J. McCarthy got traded from the Vikings to the Giants, he called it "a shock" but also "an opportunity to take advantage of."When Cam Skattebo received zero touches in Week 6 -- one week after a costly fumble -- he admitted he wasn't expecting the lack of involvement, but it also forced him "to kind of step back and look at it and figure out why."Every NFL player faces pivotal moments -- make-or-break situations where they must dig deep and find a way to respond. Both challenges and opportunities in one. These were McCarthy's and Skattebo's. And in their biggest moments thus far in their young careers, they made their stand."I think that's exactly the story," John Harbaugh said about his team responding. "I mean to that's the point. It tells you who they are. You might have thought before the game 'We're gonna find out about our guys. We're gonna find out about who they are.' And we did."
In his first start with New York, McCarthy threw for 252 yards and had no turnovers, and in his return to prominence in the lineup, Skattebo ran for 124 yards and a touchdown as the Giants upset the Texans 27-21 in overtime. Skattebo's 42-yard rumble -- the longest run of his career -- set up Devin Singletary's walkoff score.
Before the overtime bursts, though, McCarthy put on a laser show against one of the NFL's most talented defenses. He smartly leaned on Malik Nabers (seven catches, 111 yards), who is looking very much like he's back to pre-ACL tear form, and made several truly outstanding throws.
McCarthy completed five throws of at least 15 yards downfield after completing six last week as a sub. The 11 completions are his most in a two-game span in his career ... and he didn't even sub in for Jameis Winston until the fourth quarter last week.
This is what the Vikings had hoped McCarthy would be when they drafted him: an athletic quarterback with a live arm able to access every part of the field. For McCarthy to do this, given the circumstances -- traded just weeks earlier, making his first start on the road against a really good defense -- was shockingly impressive."It's that thing: It's guys have scars," Harbaugh said. "He has scars. He's been wounded. He's been wounded. He's been battered. But you heal stronger, and you become better because of it, so you should be grateful." Skattebo, meanwhile, ran over, around and through Houston's defense. His 7.3 yards per carry represented the best of his career, and he credited the offensive line for opening up holes; his 65 yards before contact were the most in any game in his career. He also told the team's postgame show that he had ball security on his mind, which wasn't the case against Washington.
The common denominator between McCarthy's and Skattebo's performances? Harbaugh, the man who gave both players opportunities: Skattebo an opportunity to learn, McCarthy an opportunity, period.The end of Harbaugh's time in Baltimore was defined by disappointment. After 18 years and a Super Bowl triumph with the Ravens, Harbaugh watched a Tyler Loop field goal sail wide in Week 18 last year, ending Baltimore's playoff hopes. He never got Lamar Jackson and co. over the hump. His reputation took a major hit in turn.But perhaps it took too big of a hit. This coach has won 184 games. He won double-digit games 11 times in 18 years in Baltimore. That included his first year, when he turned a 5-11 team from 2007 to an 11-5 team in 2008. He knows how to build a winner and sustain a winner.
The early returns are that he's doing it again in New York. The Giants are 4-2-1, two wins ahead of anyone else in the NFC East. The Giants have won with Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston and, now, McCarthy as starting quarterback. They're the first team since the 2016 Patriots to have three different winning starting quarterbacks within the first seven games of the year.And this one meant as much as any regular-season win has. Just look at how Harbaugh reacted:
"I'm having a lot of fun," Harbaugh said, a smile coming to his face. "I'm having a lot of fun. There was a little dancing in the locker room."
McCarthy used that "fun" word, too."It was a lot of fun. So much fun to be out there playing football, but with this group, it makes it that much more fun, that's for sure."And that's what these Giants were Sunday: fun. Fun to see McCarthy shining in a spot no one could have envisioned him in just a few weeks ago, when he was sitting on the Vikings' bench. Fun to see Skattebo ripping off big gains and Nabers making wild catches. Fun to see Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux wreaking havoc.Fun to see that, after losing their quarterback in Week 2, they're still playing well and still winning. Everything could have gone off course after Dart's injury. Instead, the Giants will head into their bye with their heads held high, in first place in their division and with meaningful football ahead.
"It's a reward," Harbaugh said. "Now you've got to make something of it. It doesn't mean anything if you don't build on it, right? Well, it means something, but it doesn't mean we're gonna win a championship yet. It means we have an opportunity."... We're gonna be in this thing until the end."

        Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is making his return this week against the Carolina Panthers, after missing the last three games with a right thumb injury. And to make his return to action a little easier, he got an assist from a World Series team. Mayfield will wear a custom glove to help protect his throwing thumb, given to him by the Tampa Bay Rays training staff. The Buccaneers reached out to Nike, which made a custom protective glove for MLB star Mike Trout. The inquiry led the Rays, who are playing in the 2026 World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, to offer to help.The Rays sent a member of the equipment staff to the Bucs' facility to meet with Mayfield and make the glove for him. According to the Tampa Bay Times, clubhouse attendant Nick Bond modified a wide receiver glove by removing material around the thumb and adding an insert for protection. Two gloves were made: one with hard plastic and another resembling a soft cast.
Here is a look at the glove:
"[It's] not restricting because it's on the backside. ... For me, just getting used to it. I don't feel the difference. It's just like me wearing a glove," Mayfield said. Rays equipment manager Tyler Wall spoke to the abilities of Bond and their plan for the glove. "I said our guy can do anything," Wall said. "They worked together and kind of Frankensteined a glove together, working with their trainers, Baker and Nick Bond. [It's] not hard enough to restrict the thumb but enough for protection. So he built a pocket around the thumb and inserted it. It worked pretty good."
The Rays are currently down 2-0 against the Brewers, but even as they prepared for this weekend's games, they were able to extend some help to another Tampa team.The Buccaneers sit at 1-5 on the season, losing two of the three games Mayfield missed. But their poor record is not all because of Mayfield's absence. Even when he was playing, Mayfield was struggling, with 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. The season's hope isn't over quite yet, thanks to the rest of the NFC South struggling as well.The Panthers, who Mayfield played for in 2022, lead the division at 3-2, followed by the 2-4 Atlanta Falcons and 2-4 New Orleans Saints.

title: NFL Week 7 winners and losers: Cam Skattebo, J.J. McCarthy lift Giants, Aaron Glenn's seat heats up, Falcons take down 49ers - CBS Sports
description: One of the New York teams is in much better shape than the other. Plus, what happened to the Panthers?
body:
One of the New York teams is in much better shape than the other. Plus, what happened to the Panthers?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 25, 2026

        Week 7 in the NFL placed a wedge between the two New York teams. The Giants are riding high as the leaders of the NFC East, while the Jets reached a new low with a loss to the league's worst team. Cam Skattebo and J.J. McCarthy are heralded this week for keeping the Giants' offense in surprisingly excellent shape, and at the same time, Aaron Glenn is feeling the heat from the Jets' fanbase amid a 2-5 start to the campaign.That dichotomy encapsulates the highs and lows of Week 7. This deep into the season, teams that suffer bad losses can feel truly helpless. The Jets are not alone in their misery as other squads slipped multiple games below .500 with them. And on the flip side, those who are at or near the top of their division should feel as though they will compete for a playoff berth.Here are the biggest winners and losers from Sunday's action in the NFL.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winners: Cam Skattebo, J.J. McCarthy and the GiantsCall it the Cam Skattebo redemption game. One week after John Harbaugh relegated him to the bench, the New York Giants running back amassed 124 yards and a touchdown in a bounce-back effort against the Houston Texans. He broke loose for a 42-yarder, which set the Giants up to win in overtime. Plus, it was the first 100-yard game of his career. Skattebo also held onto the ball, which should put him back in his coach's good graces after he opened the year tied for the most fumbles by a non-quarterback through six weeks.
It also seems that the Giants have a quarterback. Those who panned the trade for J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury could not have foreseen such a brilliant start to McCarthy's tenure in New York. Last week, he passed for 243 yards in a single quarter. This week, the oft-criticized former first-round pick went a clean 20-for-28 for 252 yards.
This is McCarthy's fifth win in as many starts dating back to his time as the Minnesota Vikings' No. 1 quarterback. If he can keep it up, this is precisely the kind of upside the Giants bet on when they made the low-risk investment in McCarthy. They can win with him and more than salvage a season that could have been lost when their Week 1 starter had his campaign cut short.With the win, the Giants are 4-2-1 and are the only team in the NFC East with a winning record. When Week 7 is complete, they will hold a 1.5-point lead in the division. Someone has to win the worst division in the NFL, and the Giants thus far are the top candidate to do so.
        
            
                Cam Skattebo redemption game: Giants RB returns with stellar performance after benching
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Aaron Glenn's job securityIt is never a good look to be the team on the losing end of a winless opponent's first victory. The Jets were on the wrong side of the 28-25 result at MetLife Stadium.
The New York faithful booed their team off the field at halftime and were less than pleased two quarters later. The angst directed toward coach Aaron Glenn is palpable, and the pressure on him has never been higher. Following back-to-back losses and perhaps the most disappointing defeat of his tenure, there is very little he can sell that his fanbase would buy. If he is fired at some point this year, this is the kind of game that will explain his ouster.The Jets are now 2-5 and will be underdogs in at least two of their next three games: at home against the Las Vegas Raiders, on the road at the Kansas City Chiefs and back home to face the Buffalo Bills. This could get quite a bit worse before it gets better.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: FalconsGood luck making sense of the Atlanta Falcons, because this might be the league's most up-and-down team. When it all clicks as it did in Week 7, the star talent is obvious, and they can beat anyone. This is also the same team that lost by 31 points to the Carolina Panthers earlier in the year and entered Sunday on a two-game losing streak. The 29-20 upset of the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers was one of those boom games and is now the best victory in the NFL this season.
The formula by which the Falcons secured the impressive win highlighted exactly why they are among 2026's most pleasant surprises. Michael Penix Jr. threw three touchdown passes and continues to show flashes of being a potential franchise quarterback. And the defense forced four turnovers and remains a stunningly effective unit despite the absences of James Pearce Jr. and Jalon Walker. Pearce will be back from suspension on Nov. 8 and should take the group to even greater heights. The Falcons may well be the No. 1 team in the NFC South by then.NFC South standings1. Panthers (3-3)2. Falcons (3-4)T-3. Buccaneers (2-5)T-3. Saints (2-5)
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Everything about the PanthersAll the Carolina Panthers needed to do to maintain a commanding lead in the NFC South was beat the division's worst team at home. That should not be too big of an ask for a squad with a dark horse MVP contender in Bryce Young, right? Apparently not, because the Panthers not only failed to take care of business against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers but also lost in devastating fashion by 30 points. It was a complete no-show from Dave Canales' team, which fell behind by 27 points at halftime after surrendering a 26-point second quarter to the Buccaneers.This was a chance to effectively put the Buccaneers in a coffin and separate from a New Orleans Saints team that lost earlier in the day in Paris. A win was also necessary to stay a couple of steps ahead of the dangerous Atlanta Falcons, who pulled off an upset of the San Francisco 49ers. The opportunity passed them by as the NFL's sixth-worst run defense allowed a whopping 258 yards to Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell, Sean Tucker and the rest of the Tampa Bay attack.
The Panthers also lost veteran offensive lineman Taylor Moton to a fractured fibula. The starting right tackle is out indefinitely, Canales said after the game.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winners: Jeff Hafley and the DolphinsThey are on the board. The Miami Dolphins have their first win of the season, and Jeff Hafley has his first victory as an NFL head coach. Now, no longer will they have to listen to questions about whether they will become the league's first 0-17 team.Hafley deserves credit for his decision-making at the end of the game. Recognizing that his team had nothing to lose, he left the offense on the field on fourth-and-short inside the final two minutes rather than electing to punt and put the onus on the defense to protect a three-point lead. Malik Willis rewarded him with a game-sealing conversion on a QB sneak and put him in the win column for the first time in his career. That capped off a banner day for a previously downtrodden offense on which Willis passed for two touchdowns, and Ollie Gordon II ran for 103 yards and a score of his own.
The Los Angeles Chargers, who were on bye this week, are the only remaining winless team at 0-6.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Tank DellPrior to Sunday, the last time Tank Dell suited up for an NFL game was Dec. 21, 2024. It had been nearly two full years since his last outing. He went 673 days without a catch. A devastating injury in that late-2024 contest saw Dell dislocate his knee, sustain meniscus damage, and tear his ACL, MCL and LCL. He required multiple surgeries and faced an uncertain future as a football player. And then he finally got healthy. Dell made his season debut in the Texans' loss and announced his return in emphatic style.While he only made one catch in his first game back, Dell got into the open field for a 43-yard gain. It was the longest play from scrimmage by either team.
Dell faces heavy competition for targets in a Houston wide receiver group that is suddenly much deeper than it was just a couple of weeks ago. His role is unclear with Marvin Harrison Jr. arriving earlier this month as a prime candidate No. 2 option behind Nico Collins. The main concern for Dell after so much time away from the field, though, is simply to be available.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Ravens' second-half effortWhen they returned to the locker room at halftime, the Baltimore Ravens held a 13-0 lead over the division rival Cincinnati Bengals. Their defense had forced punts on three drives, and the half expired on their fourth. Tyler Huntley had moved the ball effectively with scoring drives of 18 plays and 13 plays. But then everything flipped.Here is the Ravens' second-half drive chart:PuntTurnover on downsPuntInterceptionTurnover on downsEnd of gameAll the while, the Bengals scored touchdowns on every second-half possession save for their last. Joe Burrow passed for four scores in the final two quarters.
Baltimore simply needs Lamar Jackson back in its lineup. It is just 1-2 without him and now stands in last place in the AFC North by a half game. Jackson returned to practice this week, so it looks as though he should be recovered from his high ankle sprain in time to suit up in Week 8. This is not the first time a Jackson injury caused the Ravens to slip into the danger zone, but fortunately, it is still early enough in the season that they should be in good shape if he can stay on the field from this point forward.
